thread:
maria: Heads up — I found a handful of KMS-enveloped objects in partner-prod-bucket that reference an old wrapping key that no longer exists in our KMS. Could block restores for those artifacts :warning:

maria: Example object metadata I pulled:
```json
{
  "name": "partners/ingest/2025-03-18/artifact-abc.tar.gz",
  "envelope": { "wrap_key": "projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/partner-wrap/cryptoKeys/old-wrap-key" }
}
```

maria: The objects are still encrypted with the envelope metadata pointing to the deleted key id. @kevin can you triage? I don't want us to start any mass decrypts without a plan. :eyes:

kevin: on it — is this only in partner-prod-bucket or anywhere else?

maria: I grepped metadata for that key name across GCS prefixes and found ~12 objects across partner-prod-bucket and partner-archive. timestamps around 2025-03-18..2025-03-21.

sam: if the KMS key is actually deleted we can't decrypt those envelopes anymore unless we still have the plaintext somewhere. Do we have backups or original artifacts stored elsewhere?

maria: Not that I can see. That's why I posted early.

jen: We need to treat this as a secrets/credential incident surface: the service account that uploaded those objects had broad perms at the time. I want a quick RBAC check on svc-account-partner-uploader and any cross-project IAM grants. I'll loop in compliance if we need to permit any temporary decrypt.

secops-bot: Alert — kms.key.deleted event detected for key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/partner-wrap/cryptoKeys/old-wrap-key (2025-03-22T03:12:05Z)

kevin: plan proposal: 1) find all objects whose envelope.wrap_key matches the deleted key 2) if we have no primary plaintext, request data-owner approval for controlled decrypt+rewrap 3) run a one-off decrypt job inside VPC with ephemeral node (no internet egress), decrypt to memory stream, re-encrypt with new partner-wrap-v2 key, replace object atomically and log checksums 4) audit IAM changes and remove any lingering overly-broad grants

maria: + add: snapshot current object hashes to a safe audit bucket (readonly to secops/legal) before any mutate. Also create a Csuite-safe summary for legal/compliance.

jen: I can get legal/compliance approval for controlled decrypt if you provide the list of object paths + risk justification. Also need a documented runbook entry for how we did the decrypt/rewrap.

sam: technical notes — to avoid writing plaintext to disk, we should stream through a small GKE job. Pseudocode:
```bash
gsutil cat gs://partner-prod-bucket/path/to/object | \
  docker run --rm -i rewrap-tool \
    --src-kms=old-wrap-key --dst-kms=partner-wrap-v2 > /dev/null
```
But since old-wrap-key is deleted, the rewrap-tool must be run on a node that has access to a KMS hack (i.e., an HSM snapshot) — which we DON'T have. So we actually need to pull plaintext from the original producer or backups.

kevin: so two forks: A) if producer still has original plaintext, request they repush re-encrypted with partner-wrap-v2 B) if not, recover plaintext from backups (if available) and follow controlled decrypt path. If neither exists, mark these artifacts as unrecoverable and log impact.

maria: I just ran a quick search command to get full list of objects — dropping here so we can triage quickly:
```bash
# list objects with envelope metadata containing 'old-wrap-key'
gsutil ls -r gs://partner-prod-bucket/** | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c "gsutil stat {} | grep -i 'old-wrap-key' && echo {}"
```
Outputs ~12 paths — will paste the full list into the incident ticket.

kevin: I'll own the discovery sweep and generate a CSV. ETA 45 mins.

jen: I'll start the compliance approval thread and create a ticket in JIRA (SEC-1426). Need the CSV + business owner sign-off.

sam: I'll prepare an ephemeral rewrap job template (GKE job + minimal SA permissions) and a terraform snippet to revoke the job's SA after use. Keep it locked down to the rewrap key only.

maria: RBAC action: audit point — check for IAM binding drift that might have allowed partner to upload with broad perms. @kevin can you include an IAM delta in the CSV? e.g., run `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` for affected projects and diff against snapshot from 2025-03-01.

kevin: yep, will include IAM diffs and KMS admin changes. Also adding a query to read Cloud Audit Logs to show who deleted the key: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyRingService.DeleteCryptoKey\"' --limit 10`

jen: If we need to rotate service account keys as a precaution, let's do that after we have the recovery plan. Legal wants minimal exposure window.

maria: action list so far:
- kevin: discovery CSV + IAM diff + who-deleted-log (ETA 45m)
- jen: compliance/legal approval + JIRA ticket (starting now)
- sam: rewrap job template + SA hardening terraform snippet (ETA 2h)
- maria: paste object list + checksums to ticket and prepare audit snapshot (ETA 30m)

kevin: started the sweep. found two objects in partner-archive that also reference the key. uploading CSV to SEC-1426 now.

jen: legal pinged — they want business owner confirmation before we ever decrypt. Also asked for the intended final state (rewrap in place vs replace).

maria: business owner is @partner-integrations (I'll ping them).

partner-integrations: acknowledged. we'll check our internal backups and confirm within 6 hours.

maria: thanks all. keep thread updated. if we get a go for controlled decrypt I'll coordinate the change window and notify oncall. If we get no backups and business owner can't provide plaintext, we'll mark artifacts as unrecoverable and close out with mitigations (remove IAM exposure, add preventive controls). :white_check_mark:
